info.name: OnChainRisk Sandbox API
info.description:
Public sandbox tier — integration testing against real OnChainRisk API.

**Setup (one-time, via dashboard — NOT via this collection):**
1. Sign up at https://onchainrisk.io/register (CAPTCHA required)
2. Dashboard → API Keys → Create sandbox key (1 max for free tier)
3. Copy the key (shown once)
4. In Postman: set env var `sandbox_api_key` to your key

All requests here use that key via `Authorization: Bearer {{sandbox_api_key}}`. Key management (create/rotate/revoke) lives in the dashboard — not exposed to sandbox because the self-service flow is intentional.

**Sandbox gates expensive fields** — responses match paid shape but `crossChain`, `tokenFlow`, `clusters`, `honeypot`, etc. are always `null`/`[]`. See `_sandbox.gated_fields[]` in every response for the authoritative list.

variable.description: Your sandbox API key. New sandbox keys use the ocr_test_ prefix; legacy sandbox keys may still carry ocr_live_ and continue to authenticate as sandbox. Create one in the dashboard: https://onchainrisk.io/dashboard/api-keys
Light demo address — runs fast. Swap to your own for real integration testing.
Auto-populated from GET /api/investigations (first item). Or run POST /api/investigate first.
Auto-populated when you run POST /api/v1/check (sync path) or POST /api/v1/multichain/analyze (async). Source: response.data.reportId.
USDC on Ethereum — safe honeypot/security test subject.
Auto-populated when you run POST /api/watchlist. Source: response.data.id.

item.name: 1. Check address — POST /api/v1/check

request.description:
Two documented fixture inputs change only the EXECUTION, never the contract:

  - {{fixture_address}} -> synchronous 200 (check-eth-735-v1)
  - {{fixture_async_success_address}} -> 202 async lifecycle reaching complete (check-eth-735-async-success-v1)
  - {{fixture_async_failed_address}} -> 202 async lifecycle reaching failed (check-eth-735-async-failed-v1)

Every other address runs real bounded analysis and returns 200. There is NO request flag.

On a 202 the test script captures `reportId` into a collection variable, so requests 4 and 5
are runnable immediately afterwards. Ownership is the OWNING ACCOUNT: any sandbox key on the
same account may poll and retrieve that reportId — the literal key here is a convenience,
not a requirement.

item.name: 2. Graph preview — POST /api/v1/sandbox/graph/expand

request.description: Cheap sandbox graph preview. Depth 1, last 7 days, ≤20 nodes, ≤30 edges. Aggregated counterparty edges in the same shape as paid /api/graph/expand. No report persistence, no usage row, no credit charge. Upgrade for full historical graph expansion.

item.name: 3. Quota — GET /api/v1/usage

request.description: Quota and rate-limit introspection. Sandbox keys are accepted here and report `key_type: "sandbox"`. This is the supported public replacement for the internal account endpoints — no profile or account data is returned.

item.name: 4. Poll status — GET /api/v1/check/status/{reportId}

request.description: Re-send to watch the lifecycle advance: queued, then analyzing after 2s, then a terminal status after 6s. 404 after 3600s, and for any id the calling account does not own.

item.name: 5. Retrieve report — GET /api/reports/{id}

request.description: Before completion this returns a LIGHTWEIGHT 200 body — including `failed`, which is HTTP 200 with `status: failed` and `errorMessage` populated, not a 4xx. Once `status` is `complete` it returns the full AnalysisResult.

item.name: 6. GET /api/v1/check/{address}

request.description: Bounded sandbox analysis of the address in the path. Real narrowed analysis, no billing.

item.name: 7. POST /api/v1/check/deep

request.description: Deterministic fixture peel chain. Post 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000735d00 to get the null (no-chain) state.

item.name: 8. POST /api/v1/token/check

request.description: Deterministic fixture sections. Post 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000735710 for a non-ok honeypot status, where isHoneypot is null.

item.name: 9. POST /api/v1/token/check/stream

request.description: Simulated SSE. Unnamed data: frames for tokenMeta, honeypot, topHolders, tokenScore, then {"type":"done"}, then close.

item.name: 10. POST /api/v1/block/analyze

request.description: Deterministic fixture MEV result. Post blockNumber 735735 for the empty-block state.

item.name: 11. POST /api/v1/multichain/scan

request.description: Deterministic fixture multi-chain summary.

item.name: 12. POST /api/v1/multichain/analyze

request.description: Accepts a simulated lifecycle: 202 with an INTEGER reportId. Each call starts a new one — no dedupe. Post 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000735f02 for the failing lifecycle.

item.name: 13. GET /api/v1/multichain/analyze/{reportId}

request.description: Polls the lifecycle accepted above: analyzing, then complete (or failed). The terminal analytical values are SYNTHETIC. Unknown, unowned and expired ids are indistinguishable 404s.

item.name: 14. POST /api/graph/expand

request.description: Bounded sandbox graph, served by the same primitive as /api/v1/sandbox/graph/expand.

item.name: 15. POST /api/notifications/test

request.description: Simulated: validates the channel exactly as paid does, then sends nothing.

request.description: Creates (or upserts) an ephemeral sandbox label and captures its id. Up to 100 live labels; each write resets a 24h expiry.

item.name: 17. GET /api/labels

request.description: Lists only your own sandbox labels. Add ?search= to filter on address or label, exactly as on paid.

item.name: 18. PATCH /api/labels/{id}

request.description: Partial update of the label created above; omitted fields keep their values. Resets the 24h expiry.

item.name: 19. POST /api/labels/import

request.description: Row-independent import with per-row errors, as paid. A row past the 100-label cap is reported as a row error.

item.name: 20. GET /api/labels/export

request.description: CSV export of your live sandbox labels, in the paid format. Expired labels are omitted.

item.name: 21. DELETE /api/labels/{id}

request.description: Deletes the label created above and frees one of your 100 slots. Unknown/expired/other-account ids all 404.

item.name: 22. GET /api/v1/webhook/deliveries — paid only (403 with a sandbox key)

request.description: NOT EXECUTABLE WITH A SANDBOX KEY. An `ocr_test_*` credential receives **403 `sandbox_not_supported`** with `reason: unsupported` and `upgrade_required: false`. That `reason` is this family's long-standing answer and is NOT a claim that the path is unknown — the operation is real and available on a paid key; see the paid tier. It never reaches this handler. The operation is documented here — same path, same request model, same response models — so a client generated from the sandbox contract already has the method and the types it will need on an `ocr_live_*` key. Webhook delivery history is an audit trail of real outbound deliveries. A sandbox key configures no webhook and the sandbox sends none, so there is no history to serve and an empty page would misrepresent a working integration.

exec: pm.test('sandbox key is refused with 403', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));
